   181	    def normalize(self, raw_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> NormalizedPolicyEvent:
   182	        """
   183	        Normalize retrieved Congress.gov bill data to the NormalizedPolicyEvent schema.
   184	
   185	        Args:
   186	        raw_data: Dictionary containing raw Congress.gov bill data
   187	
   188	        Returns:
   189	        NormalizedPolicyEvent object containing normalized policy event data
   190	        """
   191	        try:
   192	            # Extract relevant fields from Congress.gov bill data
   193	            congress = raw_data.get('congress', 0)
   194	            number = raw_data.get('number', '')
   195	            title = raw_data.get('title', '')
   196	            bill_type = raw_data.get('type', '')  # e.g., 'hr', 's', 'hjres', etc.
   197	            bill_type_display = raw_data.get('typeDisplay', '')
   198	            origin_chamber = raw_data.get('originChamber', '')
   199	            origin_chamber_display = raw_data.get('originChamberDisplay', '')
   200	            last_version = raw_data.get('lastVersion', {})
   201	            bill_url = raw_data.get('url', '')
   202	            
   203	            # Get latest action information
   204	            latest_action = raw_data.get('latestAction', {})
   205	            action_date = latest_action.get('actionDate', '')
   206	            action_text = latest_action.get('text', '')
   207	            
   208	            # Get sponsors
   209	            sponsors = raw_data.get('sponsors', [])
   210	            sponsor_names = []
   211	            if isinstance(sponsors, list):
   212	                for sponsor in sponsors:
   213	                    if isinstance(sponsor, dict):
   214	                        name = sponsor.get('fullName', '')
   215	                        if name:
   216	                            sponsor_names.append(name)
   217	                    elif isinstance(sponsor, str):
   218	                        sponsor_names.append(sponsor)
   219	            
   220	            # Get committees
   221	            committees = raw_data.get('committees', [])
   222	            committee_names = []
   223	            if isinstance(committees, list):
   224	                for committee in committees:
   225	                    if isinstance(committee, dict):
   226	                        name = committee.get('name', '')
   227	                        if name:
   228	                            committee_names.append(name)
   229	                    elif isinstance(committee, str):
   230	                        committee_names.append(committee)
   231	            
   232	            # Get subjects (policy topics)
   233	            subjects = raw_data.get('subjects', [])
   234	            subject_list = []
   235	            if isinstance(subjects, list):
   236	                subject_list = [str(s) for s in subjects if s]
   237	            
   238	            # Get summary if available
   239	            summary = ""
   240	            if last_version:
   241	                summary = last_version.get('note', '') or last_version.get('title', '')
   242	            if not summary:
   243	                summary = f"{bill_type_display.upper()} {number} - {title}"
   244	            
   245	            # Determine event date from action date or current date
   246	            try:
   247	                if action_date:
   248	                    # Congress.gov dates are typically in ISO format
   249	                    event_date = datetime.fromisoformat(action_date.replace('Z', '+00:00'))
   250	                else:
   251	                    event_date = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   252	            except ValueError:
   253	                event_date = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   254	            
   255	            # Determine event type based on bill stage/action
   256	            event_type = action_text if action_text else bill_type_display
   257	            
   258	            # Create normalized event using the schema
   259	            normalized_event = NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   260	                source_name="Congress.gov",
   261	                source_type="Legislature",
   262	                jurisdiction="Federal",
   263	                title=title or f"{bill_type_display.upper()} {number}",
   264	                summary=summary or f"Congressional bill {bill_type_display.upper()} {number}",
   265	                event_type=event_type,
   266	                event_date=event_date,
   267	                url=bill_url or f"https://www.congress.gov/bill/{congress}/{bill_type}/{number}",
   268	                organizations=[],  # Congress.gov bills don't typically have organizational sponsors in the same way
   269	                people=sponsor_names,  # Sponsors are legislators/people
   270	                committees=committee_names,
   271	                agencies=[],  # Not typically applicable for bills
   272	                legislation=[title] if title else [f"{bill_type_display.upper()} {number}"],  # The bill itself
   273	                topics=subject_list,
   274	                keywords=subject_list,  # Reuse subjects as keywords for now
   275	                confidence=0.85,  # High confidence for official congressional data
   276	                evidence=f"Congress.gov API data: {action_text}" if action_text else "Official congressional bill data",
   277	                raw_payload=raw_data  # Store the original Congress.gov bill data
   278	            )
   279	            
   280	            return normalized_event
   281	            
   282	        except Exception as e:
   283	            self.logger.error(f"Error normalizing Congress.gov bill data: {str(e)}")
   284	            # Return a minimal valid normalized event in case of error
   285	            from datetime import datetime
   286	            return NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   287	                source_name="Congress.gov",
   288	                source_type="Legislature",
   289	                jurisdiction="Federal",
   290	                title="Error processing Congress.gov bill",
   291	                summary=f"Failed to normalize Congress.gov bill data: {str(e)}",
   292	                event_type="error",
   293	                event_date=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
   294	                url="",
   295	                organizations=[],
   296	                people=[],
   297	                committees=[],
   298	                agencies=[],
   299	                legislation=[],
   300	                topics=[],
   301	                keywords=[],
   302	                confidence=0.0,
   303	                evidence=f"Normalization error: {str(e)}",
   304	                raw_payload=raw_data
   305	            )
   306	
   307	    def incremental_sync(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   308	        """
   309	        Perform incremental synchronization since last checkpoint.
   310	
   311	        Returns:
   312	        Dictionary containing new data and metadata about the sync
   313	        """
   314	        self.logger.info("Performing incremental sync for Congress.gov connector")
   315	        
   316	        # Retrieve the current state/checkpoint
   317	        cursor = self.checkpoint_manager.get_cursor(self.source_name)
   318	        
   319	        # Check for last sync timestamp
   320	        last_sync_time = cursor.get('last_sync_time')
   321	        
   322	        # Build query parameters for incremental fetch
   323	        params = {
   324	            'limit': 50,  # Reasonable batch size for incremental updates
   325	            'sort': '-updateDate'  # Most recently updated first
   326	        }
   327	        
   328	        # If we have a last sync time, we could filter by update date
   329	        # Note: Congress.gov API may not support direct timestamp filtering on all endpoints
   330	        # For now, we'll fetch recent items and let deduplication handle filtering
   331	        # In a production implementation, we might use the updateDate field for filtering
   332	        
   333	        # Fetch new data
   334	        raw_data_list = self.fetch()
   335	        
   336	        # Update checkpoint with current timestamp
   337	        new_cursor = {
   338	            'last_sync_time': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
   339	            'last_count': len(raw_data_list)
   340	        }
   341	        
   342	        # Save the updated checkpoint
   343	        self.checkpoint(new_cursor)
   344	        
   345	        # Return the fetched data with metadata
   346	        return {
   347	            'new_data': raw_data_list,
   348	            'count': len(raw_data_list),
   349	            'sync_time': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
   350	            'source': self.source_name
   351	        }
   352	
   353	    def checkpoint(self, cursor_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   354	        """
   355	        Save current synchronization checkpoint.
   356	        
   357	        Args:
   358	        cursor_data: Dictionary containing checkpoint data to save
   359	        """
   360	        self.checkpoint_manager.save_cursor(self.source_name, cursor_data)
   361	
   362	    def deduplicate(self, records: List[NormalizedPolicyEvent]) -> List[NormalizedPolicyEvent]:
   363	        """
   364	        Remove duplicate records based on bill number and congress.
   365	        
   366	        Args:
   367	        records: List of normalized policy events
   368	            
   369	        Returns:
   370	        List of deduplicated normalized policy events
   371	        """
   372	        seen = set()
   373	        deduplicated = []
   374	        
   375	        for record in records:
   376	            # Create a unique key based on bill identifier from raw payload
   377	            raw_payload = record.raw_payload
   378	            congress = raw_payload.get('congress', 0)
   379	            number = raw_payload.get('number', '')
   380	            bill_type = raw_payload.get('type', '')
   381	            
   382	            # Create a composite key
   383	            key = f"{congress}-{bill_type}-{number}"
   384	            
   385	            if key not in seen:
   386	                seen.add(key)
   387	                deduplicated.append(record)
   388	        
   389	        self.logger.info(f"Deduplicated {len(records)} records to {len(deduplicated)} unique bills")
   390	        return deduplicated
   391	
   392	    def rate_limit(self) -> None:
   393	        """Apply rate limiting to prevent overwhelming the Congress.gov API."""
   394	        time.sleep(self.rate_limit_delay)
   395	
   396	    def retry(self, exception: Exception, attempt: int) -> bool:
   397	        """
   398	        Determine whether to retry an operation after an exception.
   399	        
   400	        Args:
   401	        exception: The exception that occurred
   402	        attempt: Current attempt number (starting from 1)
   403	            
   404	        Returns:
   405	        True if the operation should be retried, False otherwise
   406	        """
   407	        # Don't retry client errors (4xx) except 429 (rate limit)
   408	        if isinstance(exception, RequestException):
   409	            if hasattr(exception, 'response') and exception.response is not None:
   410	                status_code = exception.response.status_code
   411	                if 400 <= status_code < 500:
   412	                    # Don't retry client errors except rate limiting
   413	                    return status_code == 429 and attempt < 3
   414	                elif 500 <= status_code < 600:
   415	                    # Retry server errors
   416	                    return attempt < 3
   417	                else:
   418	                    # Retry on connection errors, timeouts, etc.
   419	                    return attempt < 3
   420	            else:
   421	                # Retry on connection errors
   422	                return attempt < 3
   423	        else:
   424	            # Retry on other exceptions up to 3 times
   425	            return attempt < 3
   426	
   427	    def metadata(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   428	        """
   429	        Return metadata about the connector and its capabilities.
   430	        
   431	        Returns:
   432	        Dictionary containing connector metadata
   433	        """
   434	        return {
   435	            "name": self.source_name,
   436	            "type": "Legislature",
   437	            "jurisdiction": "Federal",
   438	            "description": "Congress.gov API connector for federal legislation data",
   439	            "version": "1.0.0",
   440	            "endpoint": self.api_base_url,
   441	            "rate_limit_delay:.1f} requests/second",
   442	            "requires_api_key": bool(self.api_key),
   443	            "supported_operations": [
   444	                "fetch", "normalize", "incremental_sync", "health_check"
   445	            ]
   446	        }
   447	
   448	    def shutdown(self) -> bool:
   449	        """
   450	        Perform clean shutdown of the connector.
   451	        
   452	        Returns:
   453	        bool: True if shutdown successful, False otherwise
   454	        """
   455	        try:
   456	            self.logger.info("Shutting down Congress.gov connector")
   457	            if self._session:
   458	                self._session.close()
   459	                self._session = None
   460	                self._connected = False
   461	            self.logger.info("Congress.gov connector shut down successfully")
   462	            return True
   463	        except Exception as e:
   464	            self.logger.error(f"Error during Congress.gov connector shutdown: {str(e)}")
   465	            return False

     1	import os
     2	import json
     3	import requests
     4	from datetime import datetime
     5	from typing import Dict, Any, List
     6	from affirm_policy_swarm.infrastructure.connectors.base_connector import BaseSourceConnector

     8	
     9	class CongressConnector(BaseSourceConnector):
    10	    def __init__(self):
    11	        self.api_key = None
    12	        self.base_url = "https://api.congress.gov/v3"
    13	        self.session = requests.Session()
    14	
    15	    def connect(self) -> bool:
    16	        self.api_key = os.environ.get("CONGRESS_GOV_API_KEY")
    17	        if not self.api_key:
    18	            return False
    19	        self.session.headers.update({"x-api-key": self.api_key})
    20	        return True
    21	
    22	    def health_check(self) -> str:
    23	        if not self.connect():
    24	            return "AUTH_FAILED"
    25	        try:
    26	            response = self.session.get(f"{self.base_url}/bill")
    27	            if response.status_code == 200:
    28	                return "HEALTHY"
    29	            elif response.status_code == 429:
    30	                return "RATE_LIMITED"
    31	            return "DEGRADED"
    32	        except Exception:
    33	            return "OFFLINE"
    34	
    35	    def fetch(self, **kwargs) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    36	        if not self.api_key:
    37	            self.connect()
    38	
    39	        # Example fetch logic for recent bills
    40	        response = self.session.get(f"{self.base_url}/bill", params={"limit": 5, "format": "json"})
    41	        response.raise_for_status()
    42	
    43	        data = response.json()
    44	        bills = data.get("bills", [])
    45	
    46	        # Keyword Bouncer: filter for finance-relevant legislation
    47	        TARGET_KEYWORDS = ["credit", "lending", "bnpl", "buy now, pay later", "industrial loan", "bank", "charter", "consumer finance", "interest rate"]
    48	        # Convert keywords to lowercase for case-insensitive matching
    49	        keywords = [k.lower() for k in TARGET_KEYWORDS]
    50	        filtered_bills = []
    51	        for bill in bills:
    52	            title = bill.get('title', '').lower()
    53	            summary = bill.get('summary', '').lower()
    54	            # Check if any keyword appears in title or summary
    55	            if any(keyword in title or keyword in summary for keyword in keywords):
    56	                filtered_bills.append(bill)
    57	
    58	        return filtered_bills
    59	
    60	    def normalize(self, raw_payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> NormalizedPolicyEvent:
    61	        """
    62	        Maps the Congress.gov API JSON into the NormalizedPolicyEvent dataclass.
    63	        """
    64	        try:
    65	            congress_num = str(raw_payload.get("congress", ""))
    66	            bill_type = str(raw_payload.get("type", "")).upper()
    67	            bill_number = str(raw_payload.get("number", ""))
    68	            title = raw_payload.get("title", "Unknown Title")
    69	
    70	            # Construct public URL
    71	            public_url = ""
    72	            if congress_num and bill_type and bill_number:
    73	                public_url = f"https://www.congress.gov/bill/{congress_num}th-congress/{bill_type.lower()}-bill/{bill_number}"
    74	
    75	            return NormalizedPolicyEvent(
    76	                source_name="Congress.gov",
    77	                source_type="Legislation",
    78	                jurisdiction="Federal",
    79	                title=title,
    80	                summary=raw_payload.get("updateDate", "No summary provided."),
    81	                event_type="Bill Update",
    82	                event_date=raw_payload.get("latestAction", {}).get("actionDate", datetime.utcnow().isoformat()),
    83	                url=public_url,
    84	                organization=["US Congress"],
    85	                people=[],
    86	                committees=[],
    87	                agencies=[],
    88	                legislation=[f"{bill_type} {bill_number}"],
    89	                topics=[],
    90	                keywords=[],
    91	                confidence="high",
    92	                evidence=[public_url],
    93	                raw_payload=raw_payload,
    94	                connector_version="1.0",
    95	                collected_at=datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    96	                human_review_status=None
    97	            )
    98	        except Exception as e:
    99	            # Return a fallback event if parsing fails completely
   100	            return NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   101	                source_name="Congress.gov",
   102	                source_type="Legislation",
   103	                jurisdiction="Federal",
   104	                title="Error Normalizing Bill",
   105	                summary=str(e),
   106	                event_type="Error",
   107	                event_date=datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
   108	                url="",
   109	                organization=[],
   110	                people=[],
   111	                committees=[],
   112	                agencies=[],
   113	                legislation=[],
   114	                topics=[],
   115	                keywords=[],
   116	                confidence="low",
   117	                evidence=[],
   118	                raw_payload=raw_payload,
   119	                connector_version="1.0",
   120	                collected_at=datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
   121	                human_review_status=None
   122	            )
   123

===== ./infrastructure/connectors/legislation/legiscan_connector.py =====
     1	"""
     2	LegiScan Connector: Concrete implementation for LegiScan data source.
     3	Fetches bills and legislation from state legislatures via the LegiScan API.
     4	"""
     5	
     6	import logging
     7	import time
     8	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
     9	import requests
    10	from requests.exceptions import RequestException
    11	from datetime import datetime, timezone
    12	
    13	from ..base_connector import BaseSourceConnector
    14	from .normalization import NormalizedPolicyEvent
    15	
    16	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    17	
    18	
    19	class LegiScanConnector(BaseSourceConnector):
    20	    """
    21	    Concrete connector for the LegiScan data source.
    22	    Fetches and normalizes LegiScan bills and legislation.
    23	    """
    24	
    25	    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any]):
    26	        """
    27	        Initialize the LegiScanConnector.
    28	
    29	        Args:
    30	            config: Dictionary containing configuration for the connector
    31	                   Expected keys: 'api_base_url', 'timeout', 'rate_limit_delay', 'api_key'
    32	        """
    33	        super().__init__("LegiScan", config)  # source_name must be exactly "LegiScan"
    34	        self.api_base_url = config.get('api_base_url', 'https://api.legiscan.com/')
    35	        self.timeout = config.get('timeout', 30)
    36	        self.rate_limit_delay = config.get('rate_limit_delay', 1.0)
    37	        self.api_key = config.get('api_key')
    38	        self._session = None
    39	        self._checkpoint_manager = None  # Will be initialized in BaseConnector or set externally
    40	        self.logger = logging.getLogger(self.__class__.__name__)
    41	
    42	    def connect(self) -> bool:
    43	        """
    44	        Establish connection to the LegiScan API by creating a requests session.
    45	
    46	        Returns:
    47	            bool: True if connection successful, False otherwise
    48	        """
    49	        try:
    50	            self.logger.info("Connecting to LegiScan API")
    51	            self._session = requests.Session()
    52	            # LegiScan API doesn't require special headers beyond standard ones
    53	            self._session.headers.update({
    54	                'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
    55	                'Accept': 'application/json'
    56	            })
    57	            self._connected = True
    58	            self.logger.info("Connection to LegiScan API established")
    59	            return True
    60	        except Exception as e:
    61	            self.logger.error(f"Failed to connect to LegiScan API: {str(e)}")
    62	            self._connected = False
    63	            return False
    64	
    65	    def authenticate(self) -> bool:
    66	        """
    67	        Authenticate with the LegiScan API.
    68	        Note: LegiScan API uses API key in query parameters.
    69	
    70	        Returns:
    71	            bool: True if authentication successful, False otherwise
    72	        """
    73	        if not self.api_key:
    74	            self.logger.warning("No API key provided for LegiScan connector")
    75	            self._authenticated = False
    76	            return False
    77	        # The API key is passed in the request parameters, not as a header
    78	        self._authenticated = True
    79	        return True
    80	
    81	    def health_check(self) -> bool:
    82	        """
    83	        Check if the connection to the LegiScan API is healthy by making a simple request.
    84	
    85	        Returns:
    86	            bool: True if connection is healthy, False otherwise
    87	        """
    88	        if not self._connected or not self._session:
    89	            return False
    90	
    91	        try:
    92	            # Make a minimal request to check API availability using getMasterList with minimal parameters
    93	            params = {
    94	                'key': self.api_key,
    95	                'op': 'getMasterList',
    96	                'state': 'US'  # Federal level
    97	            }
    98	            response = self._session.get(
    99	                self.api_base_url,
   100	                params=params,
   101	                timeout=self.timeout
   102	            )
   103	            # Consider 200 OK as healthy
   104	            is_healthy = response.status_code == 200
   105	            if is_healthy:
   106	                # Also check if the response contains valid JSON
   107	                try:
   108	                    data = response.json()
   109	                    if data.get('status') == 'OK':
   110	                        self.logger.debug("LegiScan API health check passed")
   111	                    else:
   112	                        self.logger.warning(f"LegiScan API health check failed: {data.get('message')}")
   113	                        is_healthy = False
   114	                except ValueError:
   115	                    self.logger.warning("LegiScan API health check failed: invalid JSON response")
   116	                    is_healthy = False
   117	            else:
   118	                self.logger.warning(f"LegiScan API health check failed with status {response.status_code}")
   119	            return is_healthy
   120	        except RequestException as e:
   121	            self.logger.error(f"LegiScan API health check failed: {str(e)}")
   122	            return False
   123	        except Exception as e:
   124	            self.logger.error(f"Unexpected error during LegiScan API health check: {str(e)}")
   125	            return False
   126	
   127	    def fetch(self, query: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   128	        """
   129	        Retrieve data from the LegiScan API based on query parameters.
   130	
   131	        Args:
   132	            query: Dictionary containing query parameters
   133	                  Expected keys: 'state', 'query', 'year', etc.
   134	
   135	        Returns:
   136	            List of dictionaries containing the retrieved data
   137	        """
   138	        if not self.is_connected or not self._session:
   139	            if not self.connect():
   140	                self.logger.error("Failed to establish connection for fetch operation")
   141	                return []
   142	            self.authenticate()
   143	
   144	        try:
   145	            self.logger.info(f"Fetching data from LegiScan API with query: {query}")
   146	
   147	            # Prepare request parameters for LegiScan API
   148	            params = {}
   149	
   150	            # Handle API key
   151	            if self.api_key:
   152	                params['key'] = self.api_key
   153	
   154	            # Handle operation - default to getSearch for bill searching
   155	            if 'op' in query:
   156	                params['op'] = query['op']
   157	            else:
   158	                params['op'] = 'getSearch'  # Default operation
   159	
   160	            # Handle state parameter
   161	            if 'state' in query:
   162	                params['state'] = query['state']
   163	            else:
   164	                params['state'] = 'US'  # Default to federal
   165	
   166	            # Handle query parameter (search terms)
   167	            if 'query' in query:
   168	                params['query'] = query['query']
   169	
   170	            # Handle year parameter
   171	            if 'year' in query:
   172	                params['year'] = query['year']
   173	
   174	            # Make the request
   175	            response = self._session.get(
   176	                self.api_base_url,
   177	                params=params,
   178	                timeout=self.timeout
   179	            )
   180	
   181	            # Raise exception for bad status codes
   182	            response.raise_for_status()
   183	
   184	            # Parse JSON response
   185	            response_data = response.json()
   186	
   187	            # LegiScan API returns a dictionary with 'status' and data
   188	            if response_data.get('status') != 'OK':
   189	                self.logger.warning(f"LegiScan API returned non-OK status: {response_data.get('status')}")
   190	                return []
   191	
   192	            # Extract the relevant data based on operation
   193	            op = params.get('op', 'getSearch')
   194	            raw_data = []
   195	
   196	            if op == 'getSearch':
   197	                # For getSearch, the results are in 'searchresult'
   198	                search_result = response_data.get('searchresult', {})
   199	                if isinstance(search_result, dict):
   200	                    # Convert dict to list of bills, skipping 'summary' key
   201	                    for key, value in search_result.items():
   202	                        if key != 'summary' and isinstance(value, dict):
   203	                            # Add the state to each bill record for jurisdiction mapping
   204	                            value['state'] = params.get('state', 'US')
   205	                            raw_data.append(value)
   206	                elif isinstance(search_result, list):
   207	                    # Add state to each bill record
   208	                    state_val = params.get('state', 'US')
   209	                    for item in search_result:
   210	                        if isinstance(item, dict):
   211	                            item['state'] = state_val
   212	                    raw_data = search_result
   213	            elif op == 'getBill':
   214	                # For getBill, the bill data is in 'bill'
   215	                bill_data = response_data.get('bill', {})
   216	                if bill_data:
   217	                    bill_data['state'] = params.get('state', 'US')
   218	                    raw_data = [bill_data]
   219	            elif op == 'getMasterList':
   220	                # For getMasterList, the bills are in 'masterlist'
   221	                master_list = response_data.get('masterlist', [])
   222	                if isinstance(master_list, list):
   223	                    # Add state to each bill record
   224	                    state_val = params.get('state', 'US')
   225	                    for item in master_list:
   226	                        if isinstance(item, dict):
   227	                            item['state'] = state_val
   228	                    raw_data = master_list
   229	
   230	            # Ensure we got a list
   231	            if not isinstance(raw_data, list):
   232	                self.logger.warning(f"Expected list from LegiScan API, got {type(raw_data)}")
   233	                raw_data = []
   234	
   235	            self.logger.info(f"Retrieved {len(raw_data)} records from LegiScan API")
   236	            return raw_data
   237	
   238	        except RequestException as e:
   239	            self.logger.error(f"Request to LegiScan API failed: {str(e)}")
   240	            return []
   241	        except Exception as e:
   242	            self.logger.error(f"Unexpected error fetching data from LegiScan API: {str(e)}")
   243	            return []
   244	
   245	    def normalize(self, raw_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> NormalizedPolicyEvent:
   246	        """
   247	        Normalize retrieved LegiScan data to the NormalizedPolicyEvent schema.
   248	
   249	        Args:
   250	            raw_data: Dictionary containing raw LegiScan bill data
   251	
   252	        Returns:
   253	            NormalizedPolicyEvent object containing normalized policy event data
   254	        """
   255	        try:
   256	            # Extract relevant fields from LegiScan bill data
   257	            # Based on LegiScan API documentation for getBill response
   258	            bill_id = raw_data.get('bill_id', '')
   259	            bill_number = raw_data.get('bill_number', '')
   260	            state = raw_data.get('state', '')
   261	            title = raw_data.get('title', '')
   262	            sponsor = raw_data.get('sponsor', '')  # This might be a string or dict
   263	            introduced_date = raw_data.get('introduced_date', '')
   264	            last_action = raw_data.get('last_action', '')
   265	            last_action_date = raw_data.get('last_action_date', '')
   266	            url = raw_data.get('url', '')
   267	            chamber = raw_data.get('chamber', '')  # e.g., 'House', 'Senate'
   268	            status = raw_data.get('status', '')  # e.g., 'Active', 'Passed'
   269	
   270	            # Process sponsor field (can be string or dict)
   271	            sponsor_name = ""
   272	            if isinstance(sponsor, dict):
   273	                sponsor_name = f"{sponsor.get('firstName', '')} {sponsor.get('lastName', '')}".strip()
   274	            elif isinstance(sponsor, str):
   275	                sponsor_name = sponsor
   276	
   277	            # Determine jurisdiction based on state
   278	            # For LegiScan, state codes like "CA", "TX", "NY" etc. represent state jurisdictions
   279	            # "US" represents federal jurisdiction
   280	            if state == "US":
   281	                jurisdiction = "Federal"
   282	            elif state and len(state) == 2:  # State codes are typically 2 letters
   283	                jurisdiction = f"State ({state})"
   284	            else:
   285	                jurisdiction = "Unknown"
   286	
   287	            # Determine policy type based on bill number prefix or chamber
   288	            # This is a simplification - in reality you'd need to check bill type
   289	            policy_type = "legislation"
   290	            if bill_number:
   291	                # Common prefixes: HR (House Resolution), HB (House Bill), SB (Senate Bill), etc.
   292	                bill_upper = bill_number.upper()
   293	                if bill_upper.startswith(('HR', 'HB')):
   294	                    policy_type = "house bill"
   295	                elif bill_upper.startswith(('SB', 'S')):
   296	                    policy_type = "senate bill"
   297	                elif bill_upper.startswith('HJRES'):
   298	                    policy_type = "house joint resolution"
   299	                elif bill_upper.startswith('SJRES'):
   300	                    policy_type = "senate joint resolution"
   301	                elif bill_upper.startswith('HCONRES'):
   302	                    policy_type = "house concurrent resolution"
   303	                elif bill_upper.startswith('SCONRES'):
   304	                    policy_type = "senate concurrent resolution"
   305	                elif bill_upper.startswith('HR') and 'RES' in bill_upper:
   306	                    policy_type = "house resolution"
   307	
   308	            # Use the later of introduced_date or last_action_date for event date
   309	            date_to_use = introduced_date or last_action_date
   310	            try:
   311	                # LegiScan dates are typically in YYYY-MM-DD format
   312	                event_date = datetime.fromisoformat(date_to_use) if date_to_use else datetime.now()
   313	            except ValueError:
   314	                # Try parsing with time if present
   315	                try:
   316	                    event_date = datetime.fromisoformat(date_to_use.replace('Z', '+00:00'))
   317	                except ValueError:
   318	                    event_date = datetime.now()
   319	
   320	            # Construct summary from available fields
   321	            summary_parts = []
   322	            if bill_number:
   323	                summary_parts.append(f"Bill {bill_number}")
   324	            if title:
   325	                summary_parts.append(title)
   326	            if last_action:
   327	                summary_parts.append(f"Status: {last_action}")
   328	            if state and state != "US":
   329	                summary_parts.append(f"State: {state}")
   330	
   331	            summary = ": ".join(summary_parts) if summary_parts else "LegiScan bill record"
   332	
   333	            # Build URL - if not provided, construct a basic LegiScan search URL
   334	            if not url:
   335	                url = f"https://legiscan.com/{state}/" if state and state != "US" else "https://legiscan.com/"
   336	
   337	            # Create normalized event using the schema
   338	            normalized_event = NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   339	                source_name="LegiScan",
   340	                source_type="legiscan",
   341	                jurisdiction=jurisdiction,
   342	                title=title or f"Bill {bill_number}" if bill_number else "LegiScan Bill",
   343	                summary=summary,
   344	                event_type=policy_type,
   345	                event_date=event_date,
   346	                url=url,
   347	                organizations=[],  # LegiScan bills don't typically have organizations in the same sense
   348	                agencies=[],       # LegiScan bills don't involve government agencies in the bill metadata
   349	                committees=[],     # We don't have committee info in basic bill data from getSearch
   350	                legislators=[sponsor_name] if sponsor_name else [],  # Sponsor as legislator
   351	                topics=[],         # We don't have topic/subject data in basic bill data
   352	                keywords=[bill_number, state, sponsor_name] if bill_number or state or sponsor_name else [],  # Keywords for searchability
   353	                confidence=0.9,    # High confidence since we're mapping directly from official LegiScan data
   354	                evidence=f"LegiScan Bill {bill_number} from {state}" if bill_number and state else "LegiScan bill data",
   355	                raw_payload=raw_data  # Store the original LegiScan bill data
   356	            )
   357	
   358	            return normalized_event
   359	
   360	        except Exception as e:
   361	            self.logger.error(f"Error normalizing LegiScan bill: {str(e)}")
   362	            # Return a minimal valid normalized event in case of error
   363	            from datetime import datetime
   364	            return NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   365	                source_name="LegiScan",
   366	                source_type="legiscan",
   367	                jurisdiction="Unknown",
   368	                title="Error processing LegiScan bill",
   369	                summary=f"Failed to normalize LegiScan bill: {str(e)}",
   370	                event_type="error",
   371	                event_date=datetime.now(),
   372	                url="",
   373	                organizations=[],
   374	                agencies=[],
   375	                committees=[],
   376	                legislators=[],
   377	                topics=[],
   378	                keywords=[],
   379	                confidence=0.0,
   380	                evidence=f"Normalization error: {str(e)}",
   381	                raw_payload=raw_data
   382	            )
   383	
   384	    def incremental_sync(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   385	        """
   386	        Perform incremental synchronization since last checkpoint.
   387	
   388	        Returns:
   389	            Dictionary containing new data and metadata about the sync
   390	        """
   391	        self.logger.info("Performing incremental sync for LegiScan connector")
   392	
   393	        # Initialize checkpoint manager if not already done
   394	        if self._checkpoint_manager is None:
   395	            # Try to get it from the base class or create a new one
   396	            try:
   397	                from .connector_checkpoint import ConnectorCheckpointManager
   398	                self._checkpoint_manager = ConnectorCheckpointManager()
   399	            except ImportError:
   400	                self.logger.warning("Could not import ConnectorCheckpointManager")
   401	                # Create a simple dict-based checkpoint as fallback
   402	                self._checkpoint_manager = type('DummyCheckpointManager', (), {
   403	                    'get_cursor': lambda self, name: {},
   404	                    'save_cursor': lambda self, name, data: None
   405	                })()
   406	
   407	        # Retrieve the current state/checkpoint
   408	        cursor = self._checkpoint_manager.get_cursor(self.source_name)
   409	
   410	        # Check for last sync timestamp
   411	        last_sync_time = cursor.get('last_sync_time')
   412	
   413	        # Build query parameters for incremental fetch
   414	        # We'll fetch bills from the current session/year
   415	        current_year = datetime.now().year
   416	        query = {
   417	            'op': 'getMasterList',
   418	            'state': 'US',  # Start with federal, could be made configurable
   419	            'year': str(current_year)
   420	        }
   421	
   422	        # If we have a last sync time, we could potentially filter
   423	        # Note: LegiScan API doesn't have sophisticated date filtering in getMasterList
   424	        # For a real implementation, we might need to fetch and filter locally
   425	        # or use different API endpoints that support date filtering
   426	
   427	        # Fetch new data
   428	        raw_data_list = self.fetch(query)
   429	
   430	        # Update checkpoint with current timestamp
   431	        new_cursor = {
   432	            'last_sync_time': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
   433	            'last_count': len(raw_data_list)
   434	        }
   435	
   436	        # Save the updated checkpoint
   437	        self._checkpoint_manager.save_cursor(self.source_name, new_cursor)
   438	
   439	        # Return the fetched data with metadata
   440	        return {
   441	            'new_data': raw_data_list,
   442	            'count': len(raw_data_list),
   443	            'sync_time': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
   444	            'source': self.source_name
   445	        }
   446	
   447	    def checkpoint(self, cursor_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   448	        """
   449	        Save current synchronization checkpoint.
   450	        
   451	        Args:
   452	            cursor_data: Dictionary containing checkpoint data to save
   453	        """
   454	        if self._checkpoint_manager is None:
   455	            try:
   456	                from .connector_checkpoint import ConnectorCheckpointManager
   457	                self._checkpoint_manager = ConnectorCheckpointManager()
   458	            except ImportError:
   459	                self.logger.warning("Could not import ConnectorCheckpointManager for checkpoint")
   460	                return
   461	                
   462	        self._checkpoint_manager.save_cursor(self.source_name, cursor_data)
   463	
   464	    def deduplicate(self, records: List[NormalizedPolicyEvent]) -> List[NormalizedPolicyEvent]:
   465	        """
   466	        Remove duplicate records based on bill ID or number+state combination.
   467	        
   468	        Args:
   469	            records: List of normalized policy events
   470	            
   471	        Returns:
   472	            List of deduplicated normalized policy events
   473	        """
   474	        seen = set()
   475	        deduplicated = []
   476	        
   477	        for record in records:
   478	            # Create a unique key based on bill identifier from raw payload
   479	            raw_payload = record.raw_payload
   480	            bill_id = raw_payload.get('bill_id', '')
   481	            bill_number = raw_payload.get('bill_number', '')
   482	            state = raw_payload.get('state', '')
   483	            
   484	            # Prefer bill_id if available, otherwise use bill_number+state combination
   485	            if bill_id:
   486	                key = f"bill_id-{bill_id}"
   487	            elif bill_number and state:
   488	                key = f"bill-{bill_number}-{state}"
   489	            else:
   490	                # Fallback to hash of entire record
   491	                import hashlib
   492	                key = f"hash-{hashlib.md5(str(raw_payload).encode()).hexdigest()}"
   493	            
   494	            if key not in seen:
   495	                seen.add(key)
   496	                deduplicated.append(record)
   497	        
   498	        self.logger.info(f"Deduplicated {len(records)} records to {len(deduplicated)} unique LegiScan bills")
   499	        return deduplicated
   500	
   501	    def rate_limit(self) -> None:
   502	        """Apply rate limiting to prevent overwhelming the LegiScan API."""
   503	        time.sleep(self.rate_limit_delay)
   504	
   505	    def retry(self, exception: Exception, attempt: int) -> bool:
   506	        """
   507	        Determine whether to retry an operation after an exception.
   508	        
   509	        Args:
   510	            exception: The exception that occurred
   511	            attempt: Current attempt number (starting from 1)
   512	            
   513	        Returns:
   514	            True if the operation should be retried, False otherwise
   515	        """
   516	        # Don't retry client errors (4xx) except 429 (rate limit)
   517	        if isinstance(exception, RequestException):
   518	            if hasattr(exception, 'response') and exception.response is not None:
   519	                status_code = exception.response.status_code
   520	                if 400 <= status_code < 500:
   521	                    # Don't retry client errors except rate limiting
   522	                    return status_code == 429 and attempt < 3
   523	                elif 500 <= status_code < 600:
   524	                    # Retry server errors
   525	                    return attempt < 3
   526	                else:
   527	                    # Retry on connection errors, timeouts, etc.
   528	                    return attempt < 3
   529	            else:
   530	                # Retry on connection errors
   531	                return attempt < 3
   532	        else:
   533	            # Retry on other exceptions up to 3 times
   534	            return attempt < 3
   535	
   536	    def metadata(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   537	        """
   538	        Return metadata about the connector and its capabilities.
   539	        
   540	        Returns:
   541	            Dictionary containing connector metadata
   542	        """
   543	        return {
   544	            "name": self.source_name,
   545	            "type": "legiscan",
   546	            "jurisdiction": "Multi-State (50 states + federal)",
   547	            "description": "LegiScan API connector for state and federal legislation",
   548	            "version": "1.0.0",
   549	            "endpoint": self.api_base_url,
   550	            "rate_limit": f"{1/self.rate_limit_delay:.1f} requests/second",
   551	            "requires_api_key": bool(self.api_key),
   552	            "supported_operations": [
   553	                "fetch", "normalize", "incremental_sync", "health_check"
   554	            ]
   555	        }
   556	
   557	    def shutdown(self) -> bool:
   558	        """
   559	        Perform clean shutdown of the connector.
   560	        
   561	        Returns:
   562	            bool: True if shutdown successful, False otherwise
   563	        """
   564	        try:
   565	            self.logger.info("Shutting down LegiScan connector")
   566	            if self._session:
   567	                self._session.close()
   568	                self._session = None
   569	            self._connected = False
   570	            self._authenticated = False
   571	            self.logger.info("LegiScan connector shut down successfully")
   572	            return True
   573	        except Exception as e:
   574	            self.logger.error(f"Error during LegiScan connector shutdown: {str(e)}")
   575	            return False

     1	"""

     3	Fetches bills and resolutions from the U.S. Congress via the Congress.gov API.
     4	"""
     5	
     6	import logging

    19	class CongressGovConnector(BaseSourceConnector):
    20	    """
    21	    Concrete connector for the Congress.gov data source.
    22	    Fetches and normalizes Congress.gov bills and resolutions.
    23	    """
    24	
    25	    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any]):
    26	        """
    27	        Initialize the CongressGovConnector.
    28	
    29	        Args:
    30	            config: Dictionary containing configuration for the connector
    31	                   Expected keys: 'api_base_url', 'timeout', 'rate_limit_delay', 'api_key'
    32	        """
    33	        super().__init__(config)
    34	        self.api_base_url = config.get('api_base_url', 'https://api.congress.gov/v3')
    35	        self.timeout = config.get('timeout', 30)
    36	        self.rate_limit_delay = config.get('rate_limit_delay', 1.0)

    39	        self.logger = logging.getLogger(self.__class__.__name__)

    41	    def connect(self) -> bool:
    42	        """
    43	        Establish connection to the Congress.gov API by creating a requests session.
    44	
    45	        Returns:
    46	            bool: True if connection successful, False otherwise
    47	        """
    48	        try:
    49	            self.logger.info("Connecting to Congress.gov API")
    50	            self._session = requests.Session()
    51	            # Set standard browser User-Agent header to avoid being blocked
    52	            self._session.headers.update({
    53	                'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
    54	                'Accept': 'application/json'
    55	            })
    56	            self._connected = True
    57	            self.logger.info("Connection to Congress.gov API established")
    58	            return True
    59	        except Exception as e:
    60	            self.logger.error(f"Failed to connect to Congress.gov API: {str(e)}")
    61	            self._connected = False
    62	            return False
    63	
    64	    def authenticate(self) -> bool:
    65	        """
    66	        Authenticate with the Congress.gov API.
    67	        Note: Congress.gov API requires an API key for authentication.
    68	
    69	        Returns:
    70	            bool: True if authentication successful, False otherwise
    71	        """
    72	        if not self.api_key:
    73	            self.logger.warning("No API key provided for Congress.gov connector")
    74	            self._authenticated = False
    75	            return False
    76	        # The API key is passed in the request parameters, not as a header
    77	        self._authenticated = True
    78	        return True

    80	    def health_check(self) -> bool:
    81	        """
    82	        Check if the connection to the Congress.gov API is healthy by making a simple request.
    83	
    84	        Returns:
    85	            bool: True if connection is healthy, False otherwise
    86	        """
    87	        if not self._connected or not self._session:
    88	            return False
    89	
    90	        try:
    91	            # Make a minimal request to check API availability
    92	            # Using the bills endpoint with limit=1 for fast response
    93	            response = self._session.get(
    94	                f"{self.api_base_url}/bill",
    95	                params={'api_key': self.api_key, 'limit': 1},
    96	                timeout=self.timeout
    97	            )
    98	            # Consider 200 OK as healthy
    99	            is_healthy = response.status_code == 200
   100	            if is_healthy:
   101	                self.logger.debug("Congress.gov API health check passed")
   102	            else:
   103	                self.logger.warning(f"Congress.gov API health check failed with status {response.status_code}")
   104	            return is_healthy
   105	        except RequestException as e:
   106	            self.logger.error(f"Congress.gov API health check failed: {str(e)}")
   107	            return False
   108	        except Exception as e:
   109	            self.logger.error(f"Unexpected error during Congress.gov API health check: {str(e)}")
   110	            return False

   112	    def fetch(self, query: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   113	        """
   114	        Retrieve data from the Congress.gov API based on query parameters.
   115	
   116	        Args:
   117	            query: Dictionary containing query parameters
   118	                  Expected keys: 'query', 'limit', 'offset', 'sort', etc.
   119	
   120	        Returns:
   121	            List of dictionaries containing the retrieved data
   122	        """
   123	        if not self.is_connected or not self._session:
   124	            self.connect()
   125	            self.authenticate()
   126	
   127	        try:
   128	            self.logger.info(f"Fetching data from Congress.gov API with query: {query}")
   129	
   130	            # Prepare request parameters for Congress.gov API
   131	            params = {}
   132	
   133	            # Handle API key
   134	            if self.api_key:
   135	                params['api_key'] = self.api_key
   136	
   137	            # Handle query parameter
   138	            if 'query' in query:
   139	                params['query'] = query['query']
   140	
   141	            # Handle limit parameter
   142	            if 'limit' in query:
   143	                params['limit'] = query['limit']
   144	            else:
   145	                params['limit'] = 20  # default batch size
   146	
   147	            # Handle offset parameter (for pagination)
   148	            if 'offset' in query:
   149	                params['offset'] = query['offset']
   150	
   151	            # Handle sort parameter
   152	            if 'sort' in query:
   153	                params['sort'] = query['sort']
   154	
   155	            # Make the request
   156	            response = self._session.get(
   157	                f"{self.api_base_url}/bill",
   158	                params=params,
   159	                timeout=self.timeout
   160	            )
   161	
   162	            # Raise exception for bad status codes
   163	            response.raise_for_status()
   164	
   165	            # Parse JSON response
   166	            response_data = response.json()
   167	
   168	            # Congress.gov API returns a dictionary with 'bills' array and pagination info
   169	            raw_data = response_data.get('bills', [])
   170	
   171	            # Ensure we got a list
   172	            if not isinstance(raw_data, list):
   173	                self.logger.warning(f"Expected list from Congress.gov API, got {type(raw_data)}")
   174	                raw_data = []
   175	
   176	            self.logger.info(f"Retrieved {len(raw_data)} records from Congress.gov API")
   177	            return raw_data
   178	
   179	        except RequestException as e:
   180	            self.logger.error(f"Request to Congress.gov API failed: {str(e)}")
   181	            return []
   182	        except Exception as e:
   183	            self.logger.error(f"Unexpected error fetching data from Congress.gov API: {str(e)}")
   184	            return []

   186	    def normalize(self, raw_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> NormalizedPolicyEvent:
   187	        """
   188	        Normalize retrieved Congress.gov data to the NormalizedPolicyEvent schema.
   189	
   190	        Args:
   191	            raw_data: Dictionary containing raw Congress.gov bill data
   192	
   193	        Returns:
   194	            NormalizedPolicyEvent object containing normalized policy event data
   195	        """
   196	        try:
   197	            # Extract relevant fields from Congress.gov bill data
   198	            bill_number = raw_data.get('number', '')
   199	            bill_type = raw_data.get('type', '')
   200	            title = raw_data.get('title', '')
   201	            sponsor_list = raw_data.get('sponsors', [])
   202	            introduced_date = raw_data.get('introducedDate', '')
   203	            latest_action_text = raw_data.get('latestAction', {}).get('text', '') if raw_data.get('latestAction') else ''
   204	            bill_url = raw_data.get('url', '')
   205	
   206	            # Extract sponsor name from sponsors list (take first sponsor if available)
   207	            sponsor_name = ""
   208	            if isinstance(sponsor_list, list) and len(sponsor_list) > 0:
   209	                first_sponsor = sponsor_list[0]
   210	                if isinstance(first_sponsor, dict):
   211	                    sponsor_name = f"{first_sponsor.get('firstName', '')} {first_sponsor.get('lastName', '')}".strip()
   212	                elif isinstance(first_sponsor, str):
   213	                    sponsor_name = first_sponsor
   214	
   215	            # Determine policy type based on bill type
   216	            policy_type = "legislation"
   217	            if bill_type in ["hr", "s"]:
   218	                policy_type = "bill"
   219	            elif bill_type in ["hjres", "sjres"]:
   220	                policy_type = "joint resolution"
   221	            elif bill_type in ["hconres", "sconres"]:
   222	                policy_type = "concurrent resolution"
   223	            elif bill_type in ["hres", "sres"]:
   224	                policy_type = "simple resolution"
   225	
   226	            # Create normalized event using the schema
   227	            try:
   228	                # Congress.gov introducedDate is in YYYY-MM-DD format
   229	                event_date = datetime.fromisoformat(introduced_date) if introduced_date else datetime.now()
   230	            except ValueError:
   231	                # Try parsing with time if present
   232	                try:
   233	                    event_date = datetime.fromisoformat(introduced_date.replace('Z', '+00:00'))
   234	                except ValueError:
   235	                    event_date = datetime.now()
   236	
   237	            normalized_event = NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   238	                source_name="Congress.gov",
   239	                source_type="congress_gov",
   240	                jurisdiction="Federal",
   241	                title=title,
   242	                summary=f"{bill_type.upper()} {bill_number}: {title}",
   243	                event_type=policy_type,
   244	                event_date=event_date,
   245	                url=bill_url,
   246	                organizations=[],  # Congress.gov bills don't typically have organizations in the same sense
   247	                agencies=[],       # Congress.gov bills don't involve federal agencies in the bill metadata
   248	                committees=[],     # We could extract from committees if available, but not in basic bill data
   249	                legislators=[sponsor_name] if sponsor_name else [],  # Sponsor as legislator
   250	                keywords=[],       # We could extract from title/summary but not required for now
   251	                confidence=0.9,    # High confidence since we're mapping directly from official Congress.gov data
   252	                raw_payload=raw_data  # Store the original Congress.gov bill data
   253	            )
   254	
   255	            return normalized_event
   256	
   257	        except Exception as e:
   258	            self.logger.error(f"Error normalizing Congress.gov bill: {str(e)}")
   259	            # Return a minimal valid normalized event in case of error
   260	            from datetime import datetime
   261	            return NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   262	                source_name="Congress.gov",
   263	                source_type="congress_gov",
   264	                jurisdiction="Federal",
   265	                title="Error processing Congress.gov bill",
   266	                summary=f"Failed to normalize Congress.gov bill: {str(e)}",
   267	                event_type="error",
   268	                event_date=datetime.now(),
   269	                url="",
   270	                organizations=[],
   271	                agencies=[],
   272	                committees=[],
   273	                legislators=[],
   274	                keywords=[],
   275	                confidence=0.0,
   276	                raw_payload=raw_data
   277	            )

   279	    def incremental_sync(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   280	        """
   281	        Perform incremental synchronization since last checkpoint.
   282	
   283	        Returns:
   284	            Dictionary containing new data and updated checkpoint
   285	        """
   286	        self.logger.info("Performing incremental sync for Congress.gov connector")
   287	
   288	        # Retrieve the current state
   289	        cursor = self.checkpoint_manager.get_cursor(self.__class__.__name__)
   290	
   291	        # Check for a "last_sync_date"
   292	        last_sync_date = cursor.get('last_sync_date')
   293	
   294	        # Build query for incremental sync
   295	        query = {'limit': 5}  # Congress.gov API allows up to 250 per page, but we'll use a small batch for testing
   296	        if last_sync_date:
   297	            # We want bills introduced after the last successful sync
   298	            # Congress.gov API uses 'fromDateTime' parameter for updated date, but we'll use a simple query for now
   299	            # For simplicity, we'll use the introduced date as a proxy for recency
   300	            query['query'] = f"introducedDate:{last_sync_date}..*"
   301	
   302	        # Fetch new data (returns list of bills)
   303	        raw_data_list = self.fetch(query)
   304	
   305	        # Record a new timestamp
   306	        new_cursor = {"last_sync_date": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}
   307	
   308	        # Save the state
   309	        self.checkpoint(new_cursor)
   310	
   311	        # Return the fetched raw data
   312	        return raw_data_list

   314	    def checkpoint(self, cursor_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   315	        """
   316	        Save current synchronization checkpoint.
   317	        
   318	        Args:
   319	            cursor_data: Dictionary containing checkpoint data to save
   320	        """
   321	        self.checkpoint_manager.save_cursor(self.__class__.__name__, cursor_data)
   322	
   323	    def retry(self, operation: callable, max_retries: int = 3, backoff_factor: float = 1.0) -> Any:
   324	        """
   325	        Retry a failed operation with exponential backoff.
   326	
   327	        Args:
   328	            operation: Callable operation to retry
   329	            max_retries: Maximum number of retry attempts
   330	            backoff_factor: Backoff factor for exponential delay
   331	
   332	        Returns:
   333	            Result of the operation if successful
   334	
   335	        Raises:
   336	            Exception: If all retry attempts fail
   337	        """
   338	        last_exception = None
   339	
   340	        for attempt in range(max_retries):
   341	            try:
   342	                self.logger.debug(f"Attempt {attempt + 1} of {max_retries} for operation")
   343	                result = operation()
   344	                if attempt > 0:
   345	                    self.logger.info(f"Operation succeeded on attempt {attempt + 1}")
   346	                return result
   347	            except Exception as e:
   348	                last_exception = e
   349	                self.logger.warning(f"Attempt {attempt + 1} failed: {str(e)}")
   350	                if attempt < max_retries - 1:  # Don't sleep on the last attempt
   351	                    sleep_time = backoff_factor * (2 ** attempt)
   352	                    self.logger.debug(f"Sleeping {sleep_time} seconds before retry")
   353	                    time.sleep(sleep_time)
   354	
   355	        self.logger.error(f"All {max_retries} attempts failed. Last error: {str(last_exception)}")
   356	        raise last_exception
   357	
   358	    def shutdown(self) -> bool:
   359	        """
   360	        Perform clean shutdown of the connector.
   361	
   362	        Returns:
   363	            bool: True if shutdown successful, False otherwise
   364	        """
   365	        try:
   366	            self.logger.info("Shutting down Congress.gov connector")
   367	            if self._session:
   368	                self._session.close()
   369	                self._session = None
   370	            self._connected = False
   371	            self._authenticated = False
   372	            self.logger.info("Congress.gov connector shut down successfully")
   373	            return True
   374	        except Exception as e:
   375	            self.logger.error(f"Error during Congress.gov connector shutdown: {str(e)}")
   376	            return False

    25	    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any]):
    26	        """
    27	        Initialize the LegiScanConnector.
    28

    30	            config: Dictionary containing configuration for the connector
    31	                   Expected keys: 'api_base_url', 'timeout', 'rate_limit_delay', 'api_key'

    41	    def connect(self) -> bool:
    42	        """
    43	        Establish connection to the LegiScan API by creating a requests session.
    44	
    45	        Returns:
    46	            bool: True if connection successful, False otherwise
    47	        """
    48	        try:
    49	            self.logger.info("Connecting to LegiScan API")
    50	            self._session = requests.Session()
    51	            # LegiScan API doesn't require special headers beyond standard ones
    52	            self._session.headers.update({
    53	                'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
    54	                'Accept': 'application/json'
    55	            })
    56	            self._connected = True
    57	            self.logger.info("Connection to LegiScan API established")
    58	            return True
    59	        except Exception as e:

    61	            self._connected = False
    62	            return False

    66	        Authenticate with the LegiScan API.
    67	        Note: LegiScan API uses API key in query parameters.
    68	
    69	        Returns:
    70	            bool: True if authentication successful, False otherwise
    71	        """
    72	        if not self.api_key:
    73	            self.logger.warning("No API key provided for LegiScan connector")
    74	            self._authenticated = False
    75	            return False
    76	        # The API key is passed in the request parameters, not as a header
    77	        self._authenticated = True

    80	    def health_check(self) -> bool:
    81	        """
    82	        Check if the connection to the LegiScan API is healthy by making a simple request.
    83	
    84	        Returns:
    85	            bool: True if connection is healthy, False otherwise
    86	        """
    87	        if not self._connected or not self._session:
    88	            return False
    89	
    90	        try:
    91	            # Make a minimal request to check API availability using getMasterList with minimal parameters
    92	            params = {
    93	                'key': self.api_key,
    94	                'op': 'getMasterList',
    95	                'state': 'US'  # Federal level
    96	            }
    97	            response = self._session.get(
    98	                self.api_base_url,
    99	                params=params,
   100	                timeout=self.timeout
   101	            )
   102	            # Consider 200 OK as healthy
   103	            is_healthy = response.status_code == 200
   104	            if is_healthy:
   105	                # Also check if the response contains valid JSON
   106	                try:
   107	                    data = response.json()
   108	                    if data.get('status') == 'OK':
   109	                        self.logger.debug("LegiScan API health check passed")
   110	                    else:
   111	                        self.logger.warning(f"LegiScan API health check failed: {data.get('message')}")
   112	                        is_healthy = False
   113	                except ValueError:
   114	                    self.logger.warning("LegiScan API health check failed: invalid JSON response")
   115	                    is_healthy = False
   116	            else:
   117	                self.logger.warning(f"LegiScan API health check failed with status {response.status_code}")
   118	            return is_healthy
   119	        except RequestException as e:
   120	            self.logger.error(f"LegiScan API health check failed: {str(e)}")
   121	            return False
   122	        except Exception as e:
   123	            self.logger.error(f"Unexpected error during LegiScan API health check: {str(e)}")
   124	            return False

   126	    def fetch(self, query: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   127	        """
   128	        Retrieve data from the LegiScan API based on query parameters.
   129	
   130	        Args:
   131	            query: Dictionary containing query parameters
   132	                  Expected keys: 'state', 'query', 'year', etc.
   133	
   134	        Returns:
   135	            List of dictionaries containing the retrieved data
   136	        """
   137	        if not self.is_connected or not self._session:
   138	            self.connect()
   139	            self.authenticate()
   140	
   141	        try:
   142	            self.logger.info(f"Fetching data from LegiScan API with query: {query}")
   143	
   144	            # Prepare request parameters for LegiScan API
   145	            params = {}
   146	
   147	            # Handle API key
   148	            if self.api_key:
   149	                params['key'] = self.api_key
   150	
   151	            # Handle operation - default to getSearch for bill searching
   152	            if 'op' in query:
   153	                params['op'] = query['op']
   154	            else:
   155	                params['op'] = 'getSearch'  # Default operation
   156	
   157	            # Handle state parameter
   158	            if 'state' in query:
   159	                params['state'] = query['state']
   160	            else:
   161	                params['state'] = 'US'  # Default to federal
   162	
   163	            # Handle query parameter (search terms)
   164	            if 'query' in query:
   165	                params['query'] = query['query']
   166	
   167	            # Handle year parameter
   168	            if 'year' in query:
   169	                params['year'] = query['year']
   170	
   171	            # Make the request
   172	            response = self._session.get(
   173	                self.api_base_url,
   174	                params=params,
   175	                timeout=self.timeout
   176	            )
   177	
   178	            # Raise exception for bad status codes
   179	            response.raise_for_status()
   180	
   181	            # Parse JSON response
   182	            response_data = response.json()
   183	
   184	            # LegiScan API returns a dictionary with 'status' and data
   185	            if response_data.get('status') != 'OK':
   186	                self.logger.warning(f"LegiScan API returned non-OK status: {response_data.get('status')}")
   187	                return []
   188	
   189	            # Extract the relevant data based on operation
   190	            op = params.get('op', 'getSearch')
   191	            raw_data = []
   192	
   193	            if op == 'getSearch':
   194	                # For getSearch, the results are in 'searchresult'
   195	                search_result = response_data.get('searchresult', {})
   196	                if isinstance(search_result, dict):
   197	                    # Convert dict to list of bills, skipping 'summary' key
   198	                    for key, value in search_result.items():
   199	                        if key != 'summary' and isinstance(value, dict):
   200	                            raw_data.append(value)
   201	                elif isinstance(search_result, list):
   202	                    raw_data = search_result
   203	            elif op == 'getBill':
   204	                # For getBill, the bill data is in 'bill'
   205	                bill_data = response_data.get('bill', {})
   206	                if bill_data:
   207	                    raw_data = [bill_data]
   208	            elif op == 'getMasterList':
   209	                # For getMasterList, the bills are in 'masterlist'
   210	                master_list = response_data.get('masterlist', [])
   211	                if isinstance(master_list, list):
   212	                    raw_data = master_list
   213	
   214	            # Ensure we got a list
   215	            if not isinstance(raw_data, list):
   216	                self.logger.warning(f"Expected list from LegiScan API, got {type(raw_data)}")
   217	                raw_data = []
   218	
   219	            self.logger.info(f"Retrieved {len(raw_data)} records from LegiScan API")
   220	            return raw_data
   221	
   222	        except RequestException as e:
   223	            self.logger.error(f"Request to LegiScan API failed: {str(e)}")
   224	            return []
   225	        except Exception as e:
   226	            self.logger.error(f"Unexpected error fetching data from LegiScan API: {str(e)}")
   227	            return []

   229	    def normalize(self, raw_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> NormalizedPolicyEvent:
   230	        """
   231	        Normalize retrieved LegiScan data to the NormalizedPolicyEvent schema.
   232	
   233	        Args:
   234	            raw_data: Dictionary containing raw LegiScan bill data
   235	
   236	        Returns:
   237	            NormalizedPolicyEvent object containing normalized policy event data
   238	        """
   239	        try:
   240	            # Extract relevant fields from LegiScan bill data
   241	            # Based on LegiScan API documentation for getBill response
   242	            bill_id = raw_data.get('bill_id', '')
   243	            bill_number = raw_data.get('bill_number', '')
   244	            state = raw_data.get('state', '')
   245	            title = raw_data.get('title', '')
   246	            sponsor = raw_data.get('sponsor', '')  # This might be a string or dict
   247	            introduced_date = raw_data.get('introduced_date', '')
   248	            last_action = raw_data.get('last_action', '')
   249	            last_action_date = raw_data.get('last_action_date', '')
   250	            url = raw_data.get('url', '')
   251	            chamber = raw_data.get('chamber', '')  # e.g., 'House', 'Senate'
   252	            status = raw_data.get('status', '')  # e.g., 'Active', 'Passed'
   253	
   254	            # Process sponsor field (can be string or dict)
   255	            sponsor_name = ""
   256	            if isinstance(sponsor, dict):
   257	                sponsor_name = f"{sponsor.get('firstName', '')} {sponsor.get('lastName', '')}".strip()
   258	            elif isinstance(sponsor, str):
   259	                sponsor_name = sponsor
   260	
   261	            # Determine jurisdiction based on state
   262	            jurisdiction = "Federal" if state == "US" else f"State ({state})"
   263	
   264	            # Determine policy type based on bill number prefix or chamber
   265	            # This is a simplification - in reality you'd need to check bill type
   266	            policy_type = "legislation"
   267	            if bill_number:
   268	                # Common prefixes: HR (House Resolution), SB (Senate Bill), etc.
   269	                if bill_number.upper().startswith(('HR', 'HB')):
   270	                    policy_type = "house bill"
   271	                elif bill_number.upper().startswith(('SB', 'S')):
   272	                    policy_type = "senate bill"
   273	
   274	            # Use the later of introduced_date or last_action_date for event date
   275	            date_to_use = introduced_date or last_action_date
   276	            try:
   277	                # LegiScan dates are typically in YYYY-MM-DD format
   278	                event_date = datetime.fromisoformat(date_to_use) if date_to_use else datetime.now()
   279	            except ValueError:
   280	                # Try parsing with time if present
   281	                try:
   282	                    event_date = datetime.fromisoformat(date_to_use.replace('Z', '+00:00'))
   283	                except ValueError:
   284	                    event_date = datetime.now()
   285	
   286	            # Create normalized event using the schema
   287	            normalized_event = NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   288	                source_name="LegiScan",
   289	                source_type="legiscan",
   290	                jurisdiction=jurisdiction,
   291	                title=title,
   292	                summary=f"{bill_number}: {title} - {last_action}" if bill_number and title and last_action else title or "LegiScan bill",
   293	                event_type=policy_type,
   294	                event_date=event_date,
   295	                url=url,
   296	                organizations=[],  # LegiScan bills don't typically have organizations in the same sense
   297	                agencies=[],       # LegiScan bills don't involve federal agencies in the bill metadata
   298	                committees=[],     # We don't have committee info in basic bill data
   299	                legislators=[sponsor_name] if sponsor_name else [],  # Sponsor as legislator
   300	                keywords=[],       # We could extract from title/summary but not required for now
   301	                confidence=0.9,    # High confidence since we're mapping directly from official LegiScan data
   302	                raw_payload=raw_data  # Store the original LegiScan bill data
   303	            )
   304	
   305	            return normalized_event
   306	
   307	        except Exception as e:
   308	            self.logger.error(f"Error normalizing LegiScan bill: {str(e)}")
   309	            # Return a minimal valid normalized event in case of error
   310	            from datetime import datetime
   311	            return NormalizedPolicyEvent(
   312	                source_name="LegiScan",
   313	                source_type="legiscan",
   314	                jurisdiction="Unknown",
   315	                title="Error processing LegiScan bill",
   316	                summary=f"Failed to normalize LegiScan bill: {str(e)}",
   317	                event_type="error",
   318	                event_date=datetime.now(),
   319	                url="",
   320	                organizations=[],
   321	                agencies=[],
   322	                committees=[],
   323	                legislators=[],
   324	                keywords=[],
   325	                confidence=0.0,
   326	                raw_payload=raw_data
   327	            )

   329	    def incremental_sync(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   330	        """
   331	        Perform incremental synchronization since last checkpoint.
   332	
   333	        Returns:
   334	            Dictionary containing new data and updated checkpoint
   335	        """
   336	        self.logger.info("Performing incremental sync for LegiScan connector")
   337	
   338	        # Retrieve the current state
   339	        cursor = self.checkpoint_manager.get_cursor(self.__class__.__name__)
   340	
   341	        # Check for a "last_sync_date"
   342	        last_sync_date = cursor.get('last_sync_date')
   343
